purpose: Proves that a single-span exact_replace which changes ONLY the targeted text (one headline) and leaves the rest of the entrypoint byte-for-byte identical is accepted by the targeted-edit-law oracle.
required_evidence: file before (full source captured by fresh-read guard)
file after (full source as written by exact_replace)
diff: span-bounded — exactly one contiguous hunk changed, all other bytes identical
absence of elision markers in new_string

minimal_example_payload.file_before:
Welcome to Acme

Same-day freight.
minimal_example_payload.file_after:
Welcome to Acme Logistics

Same-day freight.

rationale: The targeted-edit law (CD-TOOLS) requires edits during the edit phase to be localized atomic replacements via exact_replace, not whole-file rewrites. Here only the matched headline span changes and every other byte is preserved, so the oracle returns pass.
